In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the original lesion of CAH is not an important factor in determining the eventual outcome of the disease.
the original histologic lesions of chronic hepatitis are not of prognostic importance in the absence of other factors such as the presence of hepatitis B infection.
chronic hepatitis without bridging necro-sis, even if the disease is severe enough to cause cirrhosis, does not appear to be associated with an appreciable increase in the risk of death.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of cirrhotic changes in a liver biopsy is not a reliable indicator that the liver is cirrhotic (2).
cirrhosis, as determined by liver biopsy, is an important complication of chronic liver disease.
cirrhosis is a relatively late event in the natural history of CAH, occurring in 20% or less of cases.

the presence of cirrosis and death are both poor indicators of disease activity in chronic hepatitis.
